children: Turning Point Brands appointed Executive Chairman David Glazek as its next chief executive officer, succeeding Graham Purdy, and narrowed its full-year guidance.
Purdy is stepping down effective Oct. 1 for personal reasons not related to any disagreement with the consumer products company, it said Monday.

"Graham is dealing with personal circumstances that require his immediate attention, and he felt it was in the best interest of our employees and shareholders to make the difficult decision to step down," Glazek said.

The company also tightened its full-year guidance for adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization to a range of $70 million to $80 million, lowering the top end from $90 million.
The new outlook assumes "no margin benefit from onshoring manufacturing until 2027 and prolonged, higher freight costs."
It reaffirmed its outlook for full-year Modern Oral net sales of between $260 million and $270 million.
Shares had fallen 5.6% to $64.35 in pre-market trading on Monday.
